title: Decoding sparse Fourier hypotheses
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a sparse Fourier hypothesis on $ br^n$ consist of a finite family of subsets of $ in n$ together with a rational coefficient for each member of that family. For any finite list of Boolean bits, converting the list to its represented natural number and applying the canonical partial decoding for these hypotheses returns either a sparse Fourier hypothesis on $ br^n$ or no value.
hypotheses_covered: A finite list of Boolean bits
